articles.title: The Title Comes Last: Going From Bar Member To Bar President
articles.content:
The photographs make becoming a bar president look ceremonial. There is a podium, a gavel, a pin, a room full of colleagues, and a carefully timed round of applause. What the photographs miss are the years spent attending meetings no one wanted to attend, taking assignments no one wanted to own, calling members who did not return the first call, and fixing problems no one outside the organization would ever see.
The more public the title, the more private the labor. No one becomes president on election day. The election merely recognizes a record that members have watched develop over time. You become a credible candidate one promise, one project, and one relationship at a time.
A voluntary bar association also teaches leadership in its purest form. The president cannot hire, fire, promote, or pay most of the people responsible for the organization’s work. Members have clients, trials, families, firms, and other demands. They can ignore an assignment without losing a paycheck. You cannot rely on rank. You must earn trust, persuade busy people to contribute, and give their time meaning.
Start With Service, Not Succession
The path begins by showing up. Pay your dues, attend meetings, introduce yourself, and learn what the association does. But do not confuse membership with participation. A name on the roster gets you in the door. Work gives you relationships.
Choose one committee or project and become useful. Recruit a speaker. Help with registration. Write for the newsletter. Find a sponsor. Review materials. Take the assignment that keeps sliding to the next agenda. Then finish it without three reminders. If a problem arises, bring a proposed solution.
Lawyers sometimes join several committees because a long list looks impressive. Six committee appointments mean little if no one can identify what you contributed. One well-completed assignment tells the organization far more about you. Every small project is a low-stakes audition for larger responsibility.
Become useful before you try to become visible. The strongest case for your advancement should come from members who have seen you work, not from your own description of what you might do if someone gives you a title.
Move From Doing The Work To Building People
The skills that make you a valued member will not, by themselves, make you a strong president. At first, success means completing your assignment. As a committee chair, success means recruiting others, dividing the work, setting deadlines, resolving friction, and helping the group deliver. As a board member, success means putting the institution ahead of your committee, practice area, firm, or friends. As an officer, success means preparing for problems that haven’t reached the agenda yet.
Each step requires you to let go of some control. Lawyers often prefer to do the work themselves because that feels faster and safer. But the person who makes a committee dependent on one heroic volunteer has not built a committee. A leader creates a team that can function after the leader leaves.
Share credit. Introduce younger members to established leaders. Give someone else the speaking role. Invite a quiet member into the discussion. Ask who wants to chair the next project, then support that person. The strongest candidates for president do more than assemble resumes. They build other leaders.
Understand Politics Without Letting Politics Poison The Work
Voluntary bar associations have politics. Leadership positions are limited. Regions, practice groups, firms, generations, and competing priorities all seek representation. Personal relationships matter. Timing matters. Elections and nominating processes do not always produce the result someone expects.
That reality should not make us cynical. At its best, association politics is the work of earning trust across groups that do not always agree. It requires listening to members outside your circle and understanding needs beyond your city, firm, or practice. Those conversations should not become campaign stops. Listen because what you hear should change how you lead.
It is also acceptable to want the presidency. Ambition is not a character defect. Tell respected leaders that you hope to serve in greater roles. Ask what the organization needs from you and where you need to grow. The problem begins when the title outruns the service — when someone campaigns before contributing, treats relationships as transactions, gossips about rivals, or appears only as nominations approach.
A simple test of motive: if the organization selects someone else, do you keep serving? A person committed to the mission will remain engaged. A person committed only to the title will usually disappear.
The presidency is not the only meaningful form of service. Some members create more value as committee chairs, mentors, writers, or program builders than they would as officers. A healthy association needs contributors who do not measure worth by the succession line. Pursue the presidency when the role fits your skills and circumstances — not because you believe every path of service must end with a gavel.
Learn The Institution, Not Just Its Personalities
Popularity may help someone win office. Institutional fluency helps that person govern. Before seeking the presidency, learn the bylaws, budget, nomination process, membership trends, strategic plan, sponsorship structure, major contracts, and annual calendar. Understand which programs create value, which lose money, and which survive only because no one wants to question a tradition.
Study the organization’s history without becoming trapped by it. Past presidents can explain why a rule exists, why an initiative failed, or why a seemingly easy change carries hidden costs. Their experience deserves respect, but history should inform the future, not veto it.
Respect the executive director and staff. Volunteer officers rotate. Staff often carry institutional memory, maintain sponsor relationships, track deadlines, and know where prior leaders ran into trouble. A president who treats staff as a supporting cast will waste time, repeat mistakes, and damage the people responsible for keeping the association running after the presidential term ends.
Prepare For The Work Before Accepting The Title
Before running, ask a harder question than whether you can win: can you do the job well? The presidency creates another stream of calls, emails, travel, events, decisions, and disputes. It does not pause when your practice gets busy. You need candid support from your family, colleagues, and firm. You also need enough space in your calendar to serve the association as it deserves.
A successful presidential year begins before the installation. Meet with the outgoing president and staff. Read recent minutes. Review the finances and major commitments. Identify deadlines that will arrive during your term. Conduct a listening tour. Recruit dependable committee chairs. Decide which two or three priorities can produce meaningful progress and fit the organization’s longer plan.
Do not promise a revolution. Most presidents have one year. That is enough time to advance a few important goals, broaden participation, improve a system, and prepare the next group of leaders. It is not enough time to rebuild every program or place your personal stamp on every tradition. A crowded calendar is not a strategy.
Lead Lawyers Who Do Not Work For You
The president’s central challenge is leading volunteers who can decline every instruction. In a voluntary association, attention is the scarce resource and trust is the only enforcement mechanism. Define assignments clearly. Set reasonable deadlines. Follow up. Thank people. Hold volunteers accountable without forgetting that they are donating time they can never recover.
You will still face missed deadlines, divided boards, canceled speakers, lost sponsors, financial pressure, and controversies no strategic plan predicted. Gather the facts. Consult people who know more than you do. Return to the mission and governing documents. Make the decision, explain it, and accept responsibility for it. Fear of criticism cannot excuse paralysis.
Give credit freely and accept blame when the organization falls short. Praise in public and address problems in private. Make room for dissent. Once elected, you represent the entire association, not merely the friends who supported you. The office gives you a larger duty, not a larger spotlight.
Return The Gavel
A voluntary bar presidency is not a trophy at the end of a professional climb. It is borrowed authority. You occupy the chair briefly, and then you give it to someone else.
Prepare your successor. Preserve useful records. Explain unfinished projects and emerging risks. Introduce key contacts. Then step aside with grace. Support the next president without trying to serve another term from the back seat. Continue attending, contributing, and mentoring after your name leaves the top of the program.
The measure of a presidential year is not how often the president spoke or how many events carried a personal slogan. It is whether the association ended the year with stronger programs, sounder systems, broader participation, and more people prepared to lead.
The journey from member to president is not about becoming the most important person in the room. It is about becoming the person others trust to serve the room — and then leaving it stronger for everyone who enters next. The title comes last. The service that earns it should continue long after the applause ends.
Frank Ramos is a partner at Goldberg Segalla in Miami, where he practices commercial litigation, products, and catastrophic personal injury. You can follow him on LinkedIn, where he has about 80,000 followers.

articles.title: Why Oura’s Sleep-Tracking Lawsuit Is Really About Trust
articles.content:
加州联邦法院近期对智能戒指品牌Oura提起集体诉讼，指控其虚假宣传睡眠追踪功能的准确性。诉讼称Oura无法支持其营销中宣称的高达95%的睡眠阶段追踪准确性，因其戒指无法测量实际睡眠分期所需的脑电活动和眼球运动。

传统睡眠分期检测通常需要临床设备如头皮电极和眼球跟踪传感器，但Oura的指环仅通过AI分析代理信号如心率和运动来估算睡眠阶段。诉讼引用2025年《自然》杂志发表的研究，发现Oura指环在45个昼夜的数据中仅达到约53%的睡眠阶段准确性。

原告Madison Surber是加州居民，2025年以超过500美元购买了Oura Ring 4 Gold。她声称依赖Oura的宣传广告做出购买决定，若知晓准确性可能不足，将不会购买或降低支付金额。Surber代表同类消费者群体提起诉讼，要求法院禁止虚假广告并赔偿受骗消费者。

Oura回应称其睡眠阶段算法基于1200多个睡眠数据夜的测试，并在多项独立同行评审研究中与多导睡眠图（PSG）进行了验证。Oura强调其产品不是医疗设备，也无法替代临床睡眠研究，但坚称其算法基于科学证据。

消费者保护律师Shawn Collins指出，可穿戴设备公司通常通过与PSG对比来验证准确性主张，但各公司专有算法结果不同。尽管原告未明确指控，但暗示Oura虚假宣称其指环准确性与PSG相当。Collins认为关键在于Oura是否能通过同行评审临床研究支持其95%准确性的主张。

Novellia CEO Shashi Shankar认为争议核心是信任问题而非技术失败，可穿戴设备需更精确地界定其测量能力及意义。他赞赏Oura与伊利百利（Eli Lilly）的合作，认为药物级验证与患者结果的关联是建立临床可信度的强大模式。此案的进展可能影响消费者对可穿戴设备健康数据精确性的预期。

articles.title: Morning Docket: 08.27.26
articles.content:
* 美国律师协会投票决定允许法学院继续申请免除标准化考试成绩的入学要求。对重视ABA认证的法学院来说，这具有重大意义。[《ABA杂志》]

* 法院驳回司法部申请撤销史蒂夫·班农罪名的请求。[《每日野兽》]

* 高法大法官萨姆·阿利托透露，在法学院时曾对克拉伦斯·托马斯说："克拉伦斯，你当时太可怕了，我们不是朋友。" 这个爆料值得深挖。[《福克斯新闻》]

* 法学院申请量激增。[《税务教授博客》]

* 凯雷集团因违反哈特-斯科特-罗迪诺法案的反垄断规定，将支付2.5亿美元罚款。[《法律360》]

* 杰拉德·巴尔多尼工作室被判向布莱克·莱弗利支付约40.7万美元的诉讼法律费用。[《法院新闻服务》]

* 第三巡回上诉法院允许对众议员麦克艾弗的起诉继续进行。[《罗尔呼》]

（原文刊载于Above the Law网站的《晨间文件》专栏，2026年8月27日）
articles.summary:
* ABA votes to continue allowing law schools to seek variances to admit students without standardized test scores. A big deal if law schools need to care ABA accreditation anymore. [ABA Journal]

* Court refuses DOJ bid to scrub Steve Bannon’s conviction. [Daily Beast]

* Sam Alito apparently told Clarence Thomas that they weren’t friends in law school because “Clarence, you were scary.” So much to unpack there. [Fox News]

* Law school applications surging. [TaxProf Blog]

* KKR will fork over $250 million for breaching Hart-Scott-Rodino premerger notification rules. [Law360]

* Justin Baldoni’s studio ordered to pay Blake Lively roughly $407,000 in legal costs tied to their litigation. [Courthouse News Service]

* Third Circuit allows prosecution against Rep. McIver to move forward. [Roll Call]

articles.title: Today At ILTACON: Finishing Strong!
articles.content:
Welcome to the final day of ILTACON 2026!
The event saw more than 5,300 registrations, dozens of sponsors, more than 80 panels and educational sessions, countless activities, and a stacked agenda,.
Follow the links below for more on some of the sponsors you’ll be meeting:
• Neostella
• DocStyle
• Ajax
Here’s a preview of select agenda items today.
Begin the day by storing any luggage at the Magnolia Terrace. Luggage Storage will be available from 6 a.m. to 5 p.m.
The Ask ILTA desk will be located in the Delta BCD Lobby from 7 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. Complimentary official T-shirts and bags will be available in the lobby as well! Sizes are first come first serve. The swag shop will also operate from the lobby, so be sure to grab some ILTA swag. Check in and official badges will be available here as well at the ILTACON Registration Desk.
From 9-10:30 listen to the Thursday Keynote: G100/G200 Recap in Delta Ballroom A.
Today, the Exhibit Hall opens at 9 and will remain open until noon. The ILTA Authors Corner will be available from 10:30-11:30 at the Davidson Registration Desk. Publications from fellow ILTACON attendees, book signings, and more will be available. Check the Bizzabo App to see when live signings are happening.
The Wellness Window – Presented by Harvey will run from 10:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., featuring a Protein Shake Bar available in the Delta BCD Lobby.
The next set of speakers and events will run from 11-12 including AI as a Teammate: Use Cases That Drive Talent Development in Volunteer North, Automation and IT Operations – Set It and Forget It in Delta C, Escaping the Single-Vendor Paradigm: Firm-Led KM and AI Strategy in Delta B, Helping ILTA Develop Its Strategy for the Future in Tennessee Ballroom C, Legaltech Week Live in Tennessee Ballroom DE, Making Sense of M365: Choosing the Right Tool in Delta D, Managing Scope, Spend, and Surprises in eDiscovery in Tennessee AB, Secret Agentic Man: When AI Starts Acting on Its Own in Davidson North, Shift Happens: Communicating Change for All Thinkers in Davidson South, and Your Competitive Advantage: Turning Tech Challenges into Opportunity in Volunteer Ballroom South.
Lunch follows from 12-2 with the Annual Group Meeting Luncheon – Members Only from 12pm-12:35pm in Delta Ballroom A.
The next set of events runs from 2-3 including AI Across the Client Boundary: The Organizational Architecture Legal Professionals Haven’t Built Yet in Delta B, Beyond the Bar: Mental Health and Resilience for the People Behind Every Lawyer in Tennessee Ballroom DE, From COM to Cloud: Is Legal Ready for New Outlook? in Delta D, From Users to Influencers: When AI Becomes Career-Building Work in Davidson South, High-Velocity eDiscovery: How to Move Fast Without Crashing in Tennessee AB, Is It Time for IG Ops? in Davidson North, Leadership Without Borders: How Project Managers Lead Up, Down, and Across in Volunteer Ballroom South, Pioneering AI in Legal Workflows in Delta C, and What Would You Do? – Technology Trainer’s Edition! in Volunteer North.
A Press Briefing will follow in Davidson 1 from 2:30-3:30.
Another set of events follows from 3:30-4:30, which includes AI Agents: From Chatbots to Autonomous Legal Workflows in Delta D, Building Strategic Soft Skills in Delta C, Can the Helpdesk Fix My AI? in Volunteer North, Document Review Strategy Playbook: Mastering AI + Human Partnership in Tennessee AB, RAG’s Legal Paradox: When AI Search Undermines Attorney Precision in Delta B, Social Engineering 2.0: How Attackers Exploit Collaboration Platforms in Davidson North, The Billable Hour Paradox: Making Non-Billable Work Visible (And Valuable) in Volunteer Ballroom South, and The Modern Legal Leader: Influence, Adoption, and Skills That Matter Now in Davidson South.
A Small Firms Summit will also kick off at 3:30 in Tennessee Ballroom DE and run until 5.
The ILTACON Closing Reception – Final Curtain: A Night in the Spotlight will finish out this year’s conference in Delta Ballroom A from 6:30-9. Enjoy the final day of ILTACON 2026!
The post Today At ILTACON: Finishing Strong! appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Let’s Just Say This Biglaw Firm’s Feelings About Jan. 6 Have Evolved — See Also
articles.content:
